review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Known versus famous and familiar; authorship anonymity; information access, correctness and verification distinctions.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. Cambridge supports selected everyday senses. Source prose is not copied; qualified labels, intersections and graph mappings are adaptations.
review.context_policy: New concepts and assertions use U1 and unspecified strength. Literary work retains its U4 parent and receives the same ordinary authorship genus in U1. Existing home contexts are unchanged. Relative properties refer to a fixed knower, audience, respect and time; lexical antonyms do not quantify over every observer.

sense_decisions.scope: Known to a specified subject in the relevant respect, rather than necessarily famous.
Low public recognition; not unintelligibility, darkness or total lack of information.
Public fame for a disapproved act or characteristic; no individual is assigned this property.
A name or source is not given or publicly identified; public fame is a separate axis.
Presented under an assumed name; the real identity may nevertheless be known.
Identity established in the selected context, distinct from public fame.
Identity not established in the selected context; this does not imply total ignorance of the object.
A work whose author is not identified in the relevant attribution context.
A work attributed to an assumed author name.
A work with broad recognition among the relevant public.
The intersection of broad recognition and undisclosed author identity.
The literary subset of anonymously attributed works.
The literary subset of works attributed to an assumed name.
Information available to the public, whether or not widely known or correct.
Information not openly available in the stated access context; no legal classification is implied.
Incorrect information, regardless of whether its transmission is deliberate or accidental.
Incorrect information deliberately spread to mislead. Do not limit recipients to military or business rivals.
Incorrect information transmitted without an intention to mislead in the selected act.
The intersection of incorrect content and public availability.
Information intended for restricted sharing; the intended restriction is distinct from actual availability.
The selected verification status: confirmed by checking against evidence or stated criteria. No infallibility claim.
Not substantiated by the relevant check. This alone does not establish falsity.
Information with the explicitly scoped confirmation status.
Information lacking the relevant confirmation, without a falsehood inference.
The intersection of public availability and scoped confirmation.
Knowledge available to the relevant public; exclude the separate broad-education sense of general knowledge.
Knowledge generally shared in the relevant community, not literally every human and not recursive game-theory common knowledge.
Examining information for correctness or support. A check can fail or remain inconclusive.
Preserve knowledge as information and its unreviewed descendants; not every old child has been semantically validated.
Preserve the separate IT confidentiality concept and its home context; this cohort does not alter its security hierarchy.
Credibility, reliability and truth require a separate review before synonym alignment.
The broad secret record remains unchanged; do not assume all secrets are unknown to everyone.
The preserved Russian alias слава remains polysemous; the qualified canonical label selects honored public renown.
Archive the isolated famous record and preserve all three terms. No unreviewed edges or children are redirected.

review.limits: Public availability is not universal awareness, factual correctness or permission to disclose. Verification status is not infallibility. Pseudonymity does not require the real identity to be unknown. Confidentiality is an intended sharing restriction, not a guarantee that a leak cannot occur. No legal entitlement, security guarantee, political claim or statement about an identifiable person is added. General reputation, credibility, secrecy, knowledge descendants and U3 confidentiality remain queued. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Correct the mixed fame/knowledge-status assertion. Preserve all upper exclusions and explicit negations; introduce no new conflicting pair or witness.

review.collision_decision: No normalized cross-language collision is accepted for a new concept. Reuse fame, unknown, familiar, unfamiliar, confidentiality adjective and authorship families. Archive and merge only the isolated famous synonym; preserve all of its terms.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
